About Me

I am a Ph.D. student working at the intersection of deployable structures, flexible multibody dynamics, and intelligent interception. My research aims to connect folded geometry, pre-contact deployment, target interaction, and structural response within one design framework.

Current topics include Miura-Ori-inspired webbing nets for space-debris capture, geometric interception windows for fixed-wing targets, impact-response analysis, and multi-objective engineering optimization.

Deployable structures Flexible webbing nets Capture dynamics Geometric interception Multi-objective optimization

Research Focus

01

Fold and deploy

Model compact folded configurations and their transition into controllable, task-ready flexible structures.

02

Intercept and interact

Identify feasible capture windows by combining target geometry, relative motion, and webbing-net expansion.

03

Evaluate and optimize

Expose performance trade-offs through sensitivity analysis, simulation, and multi-objective design.
